changelog: v39 fixes a register-flow edge case in v38: if the installer seeds the SMTP credentials INCLUDING the recipient address (as the seeding script does), the owner's first 'Register with Cytech' press changes nothing in the secrets file, and the v38 script -- which only regenerated the device-local smtp package when something changed -- left the mail platform generated never, so alert emails stayed unavailable until the next boot. cytech_register_email.sh now ALWAYS runs the generator after a successful registration; the generator byte-compares, so unchanged packages print 'no change' and never restart (no restart loop), and changed/missing packages get written with the usual single core restart. Below, the v37 feature set (with the v38 register-button fix) this release carries: the Register button action is a native template button (button.cytech_register_email) whose press calls the register script with the current value of the 'Cytech Alert Email' field; the dashboard button presses it. (1) IDENTIFY: until now every alert email arrived with the default subject 'Home Assistant' and a body naming only the symptom, so a multi-unit inbox -- or support@cytech.biz, who receives alerts from all Cytech systems -- could not tell which system contacted them. Fix: a new sensor.cytech_device_id (command_line sensor reading /config/device_id.txt, the fleet-unique unit id first_boot.sh derives from the Tailscale hostname, e.g. cytech-34 / cytechoffice-2 -- present on every provisioned device, no owner action needed). The three alert automations now send the email subject (notify 'title') as 'Cytech SD card alert: <unit id>' / 'Cytech SD canary alert: <unit id>' / 'Cytech restart loop alert: <unit id>' and prefix the body with the unit id. (2) REGISTER: Cytech does not know the final owner of a unit, so the alert address is the missing link -- with this release the unit's OWNER supplies their own email from the unit's own dashboard: Config Files -> System Health, 'Cytech Alert Email' field, then the 'Register with Cytech' button. It stores CY_SMTP_RECIPIENT in the device-local /config/.cytech_secrets (never in this repo; USER/PASS stay installer-seeded), regenerates the device-local smtp package, and sends support@cytech.biz a registration notice naming the unit and the owner's address -- so Cytech's mailbox becomes the unit<->owner registry, and when an alert arrives for cytechoffice-2 there is an address to reach the owner at. Pressing the button again after changing the address re-registers; pressing it with an unchanged address is a no-op. The registration mail uses the device's own SMTP credentials (requires CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS seeded by the installer -- otherwise the button shows a clear 'ask your installer' message). Internal refactor: the packages/cytech_email.yaml generator moved out of ensure_email_secrets()'s heredoc into the standalone /config/cytech_email_gen.py, which both first_boot.sh and the new cytech_register_email.sh call -- one source of truth, byte-identical output.
